anatomy.title: Overview
anatomy.body: A flat triangular bone linking the upper limb to the axial skeleton through the clavicle. Its lateral angle forms the glenoid fossa.

function.title: Mechanical role
function.body: Provides a mobile platform for glenohumeral motion and a broad attachment surface for stabilising muscles.
bullets: Retraction and protraction position the glenoid
Scapulothoracic motion contributes to shoulder rhythm

ct.title: CT appearance
ct.body: Cortical margins are high attenuation with a cancellous medullary centre. Multiplanar review is useful for the glenoid, acromion and fracture planes.
ct.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

mri.title: MRI appearance
mri.body: Marrow signal varies with sequence and age; the cortical shell remains low signal. Review the glenoid labral interface and muscle attachments.
mri.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

xray.title: Scapula · X-ray orientation
xray.body: Locate the glenoid, coracoid and scapular spine on the assembled model. AP imaging in the scapular plane and an axillary view show the glenoid–humeral relationship from different directions; a lateral scapular view adds another bony profile.
bullets: Compare the glenoid with the humeral head before isolating the scapula. Separation is a study aid and changes their apparent relationship.
A free-orbit camera is not a prescribed radiographic projection. This surface does not establish a measured joint space or normal alignment.
xray.note: Original orientation draft · independent radiology and anatomy review pending. References open separately; no images are copied or loaded, no acquisition protocol is simulated, and no patient assessment is provided.

ultrasound.title: Ultrasound window
ultrasound.body: Only accessible cortical surfaces are seen as a bright line with posterior acoustic shadow. Ultrasound is not the primary modality for the whole scapula.
ultrasound.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

pathology.title: Common patterns
pathology.body: Trauma may involve the body, neck, glenoid or processes. Morphology of the acromion and glenoid can alter shoulder mechanics.

clinical.title: Clinical relevance
clinical.body: Scapular position and control are assessed alongside cuff strength and glenohumeral range.
bullets: Correlate focal tenderness with trauma history

quiz.title: Quick check
quiz.body: Which part of the scapula articulates with the humeral head?

anatomy.title: Overview
anatomy.body: The hemispherical humeral head articulates with the shallow glenoid. The anatomical and surgical necks separate the head, tuberosities and shaft.
bullets: Greater tuberosity: superior and posterior cuff insertions

function.title: Mechanical role
function.body: Acts as the mobile lever of the upper limb while the rotator cuff centres the head on the glenoid.

ct.title: CT appearance
ct.body: CT defines cortical disruption, tuberosity displacement and joint congruity with high spatial resolution.
ct.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

mri.title: MRI appearance
mri.body: MRI can assess marrow, cartilage, cuff insertions and the biceps anchor around the proximal humerus.
mri.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

xray.title: Proximal humerus · X-ray orientation
xray.body: Find the humeral head, neck and glenoid as an assembled relationship. Scapular-plane AP and axillary radiographs provide complementary views; the projected appearance of the humeral neck depends on positioning.
bullets: Use the head and surgical neck as orientation landmarks, not a template for diagnosing a fracture.

The body atlas retains the whole humerus; this lesson concerns its shoulder end. The dedicated shoulder model is cropped. Neither supplies radiographic bone density, cartilage thickness or a patient measurement.
xray.note: Original orientation draft · independent radiology and anatomy review pending. References open separately; no images are copied or loaded, no acquisition protocol is simulated, and no patient assessment is provided.

ultrasound.title: Ultrasound window
ultrasound.body: The greater and lesser tuberosities form bright cortical landmarks for assessing cuff insertions and the bicipital groove.
ultrasound.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

pathology.title: Common patterns
pathology.body: Important entities include proximal humeral fracture, impaction defects, degenerative change and avascular necrosis.

clinical.title: Clinical relevance
clinical.body: Examine active and passive range, pain localisation and neurovascular status following trauma.

quiz.title: Quick check
quiz.body: Which groove contains the long-head biceps tendon?

anatomy.title: Overview
anatomy.body: An S-shaped strut joining the sternum to the acromion and maintaining the shoulder away from the thorax.

function.title: Mechanical role
function.body: Transmits load from upper limb to axial skeleton and permits coordinated scapular rotation.

ct.title: CT appearance
ct.body: CT is useful for complex fractures and alignment at the sternoclavicular joint.
ct.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

mri.title: MRI appearance
mri.body: MRI is reserved for selected marrow, joint and ligament questions.
mri.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

xray.title: Clavicle · X-ray orientation
xray.body: Identify the clavicle on the shoulder radiograph reference, then relate its lateral end to the acromion in 3D. Focused acromioclavicular and axillary views can examine this articulation from different directions; the appropriate clinical views depend on the question being investigated.
bullets: Keep adjacent bones visible while studying the relationship. An exploded gap is not a radiographic joint space.
Do not interpret the atlas colour as X-ray attenuation. Radiographs provide limited information about individual muscles and tendons; no ligament integrity or joint stability is established here.
xray.note: Original orientation draft · independent radiology and anatomy review pending. References open separately; no images are copied or loaded, no acquisition protocol is simulated, and no patient assessment is provided.

ultrasound.title: Ultrasound window
ultrasound.body: Superficial cortical contour and the acromioclavicular joint can be assessed dynamically.
ultrasound.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

pathology.title: Common patterns
pathology.body: Midshaft fracture and acromioclavicular joint injury are common traumatic patterns.

clinical.title: Clinical relevance
clinical.body: Inspect for contour change, skin tenting and local tenderness after injury.

quiz.title: Quick check
quiz.body: The lateral clavicle articulates with which process?

anatomy.title: Overview
anatomy.body: A multipennate muscle forming the rounded contour of the shoulder.
bullets: Origin: lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine

function.title: Action
function.body: The middle fibres abduct the arm; anterior and posterior fibres assist flexion/internal rotation and extension/external rotation respectively.

ct.title: CT appearance
ct.body: Muscle bulk and attenuation are compared with adjacent soft tissues and the contralateral side where available.
ct.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

mri.title: MRI appearance
mri.body: Normal fibres show intermediate signal with thin internal fat planes. Oedema, tear or denervation changes alter signal and bulk.
mri.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

ultrasound.title: Ultrasound appearance
ultrasound.body: A fibrillar echotexture overlies the subacromial-subdeltoid bursa and cuff.
ultrasound.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

pathology.title: Common patterns
pathology.body: Deltoid injury is less common than cuff disease; atrophy may follow axillary neuropathy or disuse.

clinical.title: Clinical relevance
clinical.body: Test abduction with attention to pain, strength and axillary nerve sensory change over the lateral shoulder.

anatomy.title: Overview
anatomy.body: Occupies the supraspinous fossa and passes beneath the acromion to the superior facet of the greater tuberosity.

function.title: Action
function.body: Initiates abduction and contributes to compression and centring of the humeral head.

ct.title: CT appearance
ct.body: CT can show muscle volume, fatty change and mineralisation; tendon detail is limited unless arthrography is used.
ct.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

mri.title: MRI appearance
mri.body: The tendon should remain low signal and continuous to its footprint. Evaluate tear dimensions, retraction and muscle quality.
mri.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

ultrasound.body: The tendon is assessed in long and short axes over the superior humeral head with dynamic impingement views.
ultrasound.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

pathology.title: Common patterns
pathology.body: Tendinopathy and partial- or full-thickness tears commonly involve the anterior distal tendon.

clinical.title: Clinical relevance
clinical.body: Painful resisted abduction may support cuff pathology but must be interpreted with the full examination and imaging.

anatomy.title: Overview
anatomy.body: Arises from the infraspinous fossa and inserts on the middle facet of the greater tuberosity.
bullets: Blends with the posterior cuff capsule

function.title: Action
function.body: Externally rotates the humerus and helps stabilise the glenohumeral joint.

ct.title: CT appearance
ct.body: Assess bulk, fatty replacement and osseous attachment sites.
ct.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

mri.title: MRI appearance
mri.body: Evaluate tendon continuity, muscle oedema and fatty atrophy.

anatomy.title: Overview
anatomy.body: Arises from the subscapular fossa and inserts on the lesser tuberosity.
bullets: Innervation: upper and lower subscapular nerves
Closely related to the biceps pulley

function.title: Action
function.body: Internally rotates and adducts the humerus while contributing to anterior stability.

ct.title: CT appearance

anatomy.title: Long head and proximal tendon
anatomy.body: The long head begins at the superior glenoid region, crosses the joint and descends through the intertubercular groove before joining the muscle belly in the arm.
bullets: Proximal tendon and muscle are one source mesh
Distal biceps insertion: radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis
anatomy.note: The mesh is not a separately segmented tendon. The lower arm is cropped from this view.

function.title: Mechanical role
function.body: Contributes to elbow flexion and supination through the biceps complex; its shoulder stabilising role is context dependent.

ct.title: CT appearance
ct.body: The tendon may be visible as a soft-tissue structure in the groove; CT arthrography can improve joint assessment.
ct.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

mri.title: MRI appearance
mri.body: A low-signal round or ovoid tendon should remain centred in the groove; assess the anchor and pulley.

anatomy.title: Posterior cuff
anatomy.body: This narrow cuff muscle lies along the lateral scapula, below infraspinatus and above teres major.
bullets: Scapular origin near the lateral border
Humeral insertion at the inferior greater-tubercle facet

function.title: Action
function.body: Assists external rotation of the arm and stabilisation of the humeral head.

ct.title: CT assessment
ct.body: Review muscle size and fatty replacement on soft-tissue windows.
ct.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

mri.title: MRI assessment
mri.body: Review the muscle belly and posterior cuff tendon for signal change, loss of bulk and fatty replacement.

ultrasound.title: Ultrasound assessment
ultrasound.body: Posterior views may show the inferior cuff attachment; reliable identification requires local landmarks and trained technique.
ultrasound.note: Prototype teaching copy — verify against an approved imaging reference and local protocol before clinical release.

pathology.title: Patterns to review
pathology.body: Teres minor may be affected by cuff injury or denervation. Imaging findings require clinical correlation.

clinical.title: Clinical relevance
clinical.body: Consider its contribution when assessing external-rotation weakness. No isolated examination finding establishes a diagnosis.
